title: Sequence-aware reservoir shadow prober for continuous CI perf gating
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, sequence-length-aware microbenchmark harness that runs as part of PR checks and nightly baselining to detect performance regressions (tokens/sec and p95) with high signal-to-noise. The harness should: 1) sample representative request sequences from production traces via reservoir sampling to preserve the production sequence length distribution; 2) compress and synthesize a small set of micro-bursts that exercise model KV-cache and attention hotspots; 3) run both the candidate (PR) build and a pinned baseline in shadow mode on a tiny, dedicated CI GPU pool; 4) produce robust metrics (median, p50, p95 tokens/sec, per-seq-length buckets) and Bayesian credible intervals to flag regressions; 5) integrate results into PR gating with clear rationale and rollback recommendations.

Why: Existing CI gates are noisy because they use single synthetic inputs, inconsistent warm-ups, and lack sequence-length stratification. This leads to false positives and missed regressions for long-tail sequences. By combining reservoir-sampled sequences with small, targeted bursts and Bayesian inference, we can raise sensitivity to meaningful regressions while keeping runtime/cost suitable for PRs.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Reservoir sampling vs fixed synthetic templates: reservoir sampling preserves production distribution but requires periodic refresh and privacy review. We'll mask PII and store only sequence-length/shape metadata plus sanitized tokens where necessary.
- Sequence bucketing: split workloads into short/medium/long buckets (e.g., 1-64, 65-512, 513+). Bucketing reduces variance and surfaces regressions that only affect long sequences.
- Warm-up & KV priming: include dedicated warm-up steps to avoid cold-start artifacts; warm-up budget capped at 2s per run to keep CI time bounded.
- Hardware variance: use a pinned CI GPU pool (same instance type + pinned kernel build) and run baseline + candidate back-to-back on the same host where possible.
- Statistical gating: use Bayesian posterior over p95 delta; gate only when 95% posterior mass indicates >X% regression (default X=5%). This reduces flakiness versus single-sample hypothesis tests.
- Cost vs sensitivity: default PR runs will be 'mini' (3 sequences/bucket, 2 repeats). Nightly full baselining runs more sequences (30 sequences/bucket, 10 repeats) and update baseline credible intervals.

Acceptable outcomes: reduced false-positive gate rate by >40% on historical PR traces, detect regressions >=5% p95 with 90% recall on synthetic injected regressions, completing a PR-gating run in <12 minutes.
updates: 2026-02-24: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and QA. Agreed on reservoir sampling approach and privacy constraints. Action: Marco to draft sampling policy.

2026-03-02: Prototype harness implemented (python) that replays reservoir-sampled sequences into a local perf harness. Initial runs show stable median tokens/sec but p95 variance high on long sequences due to KV-cache cold paths.

2026-03-04: Design review with PM (Aisha Patel) and Runtime (Ethan Park). Feedback: add deterministic seeding, record full hardware telemetry (GPU clocks/temperature), and advertise warm-up steps in CI logs. Lina to add telemetry hooks.

2026-03-06: First PR-level runs on the pinned CI GPU pool (rci-gpu-small) executed. Candidate vs baseline back-to-back. Observed 6% regression on a single long sequence; further repeats required to rule out noise.
2026-03-08: Implemented Bayesian credible-interval gating. Tuned prior to reflect historical variance from 200 recent baseline runs. Reduced false positives in pilot from 3/day -> 1/day.

2026-03-10: Flakiness investigation: discovered occasional 1-2% shifts from background system updates during nightly jobs. Added CI pre-check to drain cluster nodes and pin kernel/driver versions for prober runs. Next: integrate with PR display and rollout playbook.
acceptance_criteria: PR runs complete within 12 minutes for default mini configuration
Gate decision uses Bayesian posterior and is recorded in PR comment with p95 delta and credibility
False positive rate on historical PR set reduced >=40% compared to baseline synthetic gate
Nightly full baseline job updates baseline credible intervals and stores sanitized sampling metadata
Integration test: injected 7% slowdown on attention kernel is detected by gate in >=90% of runs
notes: Privacy: reservoir sampling will store only sequence-length histogram and sanitized tokens; legal to review before first prod snapshot.
Operational: if a PR is blocked by the gate, the default action is to run a full nightly baseline and notify Runtime on-call if regression persists.
Follow-up: add a lightweight GPU-papertrail log to detect thermal throttling as part of run metadata.
Potential extension: shadow-probe can be used in Dedicated staging fleets to surface regressions tied to larger batch sizes and autoscaling behaviors.
